fact: European explorers first landed in what's now San Diego Bay in 1542, led by Juan Rodríguez Cabrillo — making it the first place on the West Coast of the present-day US to be visited by a European sea expedition.
hook_angle: San Diego was 'discovered' by Europeans before almost anywhere else on the West Coast.
source: San Diego History Center / Cabrillo National Monument (NPS)
notes: Widely documented, low risk of error. Cross-check exact NPS phrasing before final script.

fact: San Diego is often called the 'Birthplace of California' because the first Spanish mission in California (Mission San Diego de Alcalá) was founded here in 1769 by Junípero Serra.
hook_angle: Every other California mission traces back to this one spot.
notes: Serra's legacy is a sensitive topic for some communities — keep framing factual/historical, not celebratory.

fact: The Kumeyaay people have lived in the San Diego region for at least 10,000 years, long before any European contact.

fact: Balboa Park was built out for the 1915-1916 Panama-California Exposition — most of its Spanish Colonial Revival buildings were meant to be temporary.

fact: The San Diego Zoo grew out of leftover exotic animals from the 1915 Panama-California Exposition.

fact: Downtown San Diego's Gaslamp Quarter was originally developed by Alonzo Horton in the 1860s-80s as 'New Town,' meant to pull the city center away from Old Town.

fact: Old Point Loma Lighthouse, built in 1855, was retired in 1891 because it sat too high on the point — fog and low clouds often hid its light from ships below.

fact: Torrey Pines State Natural Reserve is one of only two places on Earth where the Torrey pine grows wild — the other is a small stretch of Santa Rosa Island.
